en.note: Primary language of both app records (iPhone and Mac). A reader whose language has no localization sees this one.

he.note: Written by the base writer together with en-US; the second reference for the translators (tone).

ar.note: Apple's only Arabic localization; its code carries the SA region.

zh.note: The app has one Chinese catalogue, in Simplified characters (shared/i18n/locales.ts). Apple's Chinese (Traditional) (zh-Hant) is not used.

th.note: Apple counts Thai characters like any other; count with Array.from(text).length as the checker does.

es.note: The app's Spanish follows Spain conventions (intl es-ES in shared/i18n/locales.ts). Apple's Spanish (Mexico) (es-MX) is not used.

pt.note: Decision of 2026-11-08: the app's own catalogue shared/i18n/messages/pt/*.ts is European Portuguese - 'palavra-passe' (158 occurrences), 'ficheiro' (77), 'definições' (56), 'telemóvel' (32), 'guardar' (32), 'utilizador' (22), 'aplicação' (22), 'ecrã' (10); the Brazilian markers 'você' and 'usuário' occur 0 times ('ação' is the post-1990 spelling of both variants and 'e-mail' is common to both). The App Store localization is therefore Portuguese (Portugal), the same choice as the Microsoft Store listing (store/listing/pt-PT). Apple also offers Portuguese (Brazil) (pt-BR); a reader in Brazil sees the primary language (en-US) until a pt-BR folder is added - to add one, copy pt-PT, adapt the spelling and register the folder here.

fr.note: Apple's code for French carries the FR region; the display name is just French (French (Canada) is a separate localization, not used).

de.note: Apple's code for German carries the DE region; the display name is just German.

bg.note: App Store Connect has no Bulgarian localization (docs/APPLE-PLAN.md section 7.4, ENV-FINAL locale mapping). No texts can be entered; a Bulgarian reader sees en-US. The app itself has Bulgarian. appstore/listing/bg/NOTE.txt explains this in English and Hebrew.
